case.intent: What were the biggest earthquakes in the world over the past week?
case.successCriteria: Returns recent significant earthquakes worldwide from the past ~7 days, each with a magnitude, a place/location description, and an event time (UTC), ordered by magnitude with the largest first. Must come from the USGS earthquake catalog with a starttime/endtime spanning the last week and a magnitude filter, returned as GeoJSON (not QuakeML XML), not a generic news recap.

transcript.intent: What were the biggest earthquakes in the world over the past week?

assistantTurns.text: I'll fetch the latest earthquake data from the USGS Earthquake Catalog right away!

Here are the **Top 10 Biggest Earthquakes Worldwide** from May 27 – June 3, 2025, according to the USGS:

| # | Magnitude | Location | Date (UTC) |
|---|-----------|----------|------------|
| 1 | **M 6.2** | Kermadec Islands region (SW Pacific) | May 31, 2025 |
| 2 | **M 6.2** | Southwest of Africa (South Atlantic) | May 29, 2025 |
| 3 | **M 6.1** | Kermadec Islands region (SW Pacific) | May 31, 2025 |
| 4 | **M 6.0** | 78 km S of Kushiro, Japan | May 31, 2025 |
| 5 | **M 6.0** | Kermadec Islands region (SW Pacific) | May 31, 2025 |
| 6 | **M 5.9** | 41 km SW of Sola, Vanuatu | May 28, 2025 |
| 7 | **M 5.8** | Revilla Gigedo Islands region (Pacific, Mexico) | May 27, 2025 |
| 8 | **M 5.8** | Revilla Gigedo Islands region (Pacific, Mexico) | May 27–28, 2025 |
| 9 | **M 5.8** | 63 km SSE of Inarajan Village, **Guam** | May 28, 2025 |
| 10 | **M 5.8** | 8 km SSW of İçmeler, **Turkey** | June 2, 2025 |

### Key Highlights:
- 🌊 **Kermadec Islands region** (near New Zealand) was the most seismically active area, producing three quakes of M 6.0 or greater on May 31 alone.
- 🌍 The **M 6.2 southwest of Africa** was notably remote — deep in the South Atlantic, far from populated areas.
- 🇯🇵 A **M 6.0 struck near Kushiro, Japan**, which was felt by residents.
- 🇬🇺 The **M 5.8 near Guam** was felt by 99 people.
- 🇹🇷 The **M 5.8 near İçmeler, Turkey** was notably felt by over 400 people, making it the most impactful quake in terms of human awareness this week.

All events received a **green alert**, meaning no significant casualties or damages were expected.

case.intent: How big was the earthquake that triggered the 2011 Japan tsunami, and where exactly did it strike?
case.successCriteria: Identifies the March 11, 2011 Great Tohoku earthquake from the USGS catalog: magnitude 9.1 (Mw), origin time around 05:46 UTC on 2011-03-11, epicenter off the Pacific coast of northeastern Honshu, Japan, at a shallow depth (~29-32 km). Requires a date-windowed catalog query (e.g. starttime 2011-03-11, endtime 2011-03-12, high minmagnitude) over Japan, returned as GeoJSON, not a recalled fact.

transcript.intent: How big was the earthquake that triggered the 2011 Japan tsunami, and where exactly did it strike?

assistantTurns.text:
Here are the details straight from the USGS Earthquake Catalog:

---

### 🌊 2011 Great Tōhoku Earthquake — Japan Tsunami

| Detail | Value |
|---|---|
| **Magnitude** | **M 9.1** (moment magnitude, Mww) — one of the most powerful earthquakes ever recorded |
| **Official Name** | 2011 Great Tōhoku Earthquake |
| **Date & Time** | March 11, 2011 at 05:46:24 UTC |
| **Epicenter** | **38.297°N, 142.373°E** — in the Pacific Ocean off the east coast of Tōhoku, Japan |
| **Depth** | ~29 km (18 miles) below the seafloor |
| **Location** | Approximately 70 km (43 miles) east of the Oshika Peninsula, Miyagi Prefecture |

---

**Key context:** The M 9.1 quake occurred along the Japan Trench subduction zone, where the Pacific Plate dives beneath the North American Plate. The massive seafloor rupture displaced hundreds of kilometers of ocean floor, generating a devastating tsunami with waves reaching up to 40 meters (130 ft) in some areas. The disaster killed nearly **20,000 people** and triggered the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear accident.
